newsitem.title: FINLAND: Fine papers in line with forecasts - UPM.
newsitem.headline: Fine papers in line with forecasts - UPM.

text.p: The fine paper market has developed as expected and is likely to improve towards the end of the year, Pehr-Eric Patt, president of Finnish forestry group UPM-Kymmene's fine paper division said on Wednesday.
"The market has not been weaker than we expected," Patt, who heads Europe's largest fine paper producer, told Reuters.
He was asked to comment on an announcement from UPM-Kymmene's Finnish rival Metsa-Serla on Tuesday that it would fall into the red in May-December partly due to weakness in fine paper prices. @
"We expect the second half of the year to be better in fine papers than the first half," Patt said.
He said UPM would complete price increases of about 10 percent in fine papers by the beginning of October, as the group had announced in August.
"It seems to be succeeding," Patt said, when asked whether the price hikes would hold.
Deliveries of both coated and uncoated fine papers have risen year-on-year since the end of May, he said. @
"September has been good, and most orders for October are already in," Patt said.
But he said current fine paper prices, although they have risen some 10 percent from the bottom of the cycle early this year, are still unprofitable and below the long-term average.
"The combined profitability of pulp and fine paper is not yet at a satisfactory level," he said. @
Patt also said increased deliveries of fine papers are partly due to stock-building by customers.
